checked_contracts: Rule admission requires Undefined aggregation phase, rejects DistinctAll and normalizes only exact interval SUM arguments.
The rule is ordered before DISTINCT expansion, and the ordinary fixed-point stage will revisit aggregates introduced by later whole-partition expansion.
Fresh input IDs retain original input columns; fresh accumulator output IDs remove the original result bindings before the final Map restores them.
Trait copying retains Distinct and Unwrap flags; untouched traits and ordered group keys are preserved.
Interval and Interval64 convert exactly through Int64 into Decimal(35,0). This conversion is injective on valid values, preserving DISTINCT equivalence.
Optional input casts retain absence. Decimal-to-Int64 and Int64-to-interval final casts remain nullable for overflow; empty scalar and all-null aggregate output remains absent.
The conversion is applied before aggregate state splitting, so existing Decimal partial/final aggregation and merge schemas are reused without an interval state mismatch.
Constant-size rule metadata and a generated input map reused per source IU avoid repeated normalization; the replacement Decimal argument prevents a rule loop.
The existing cast implementation explicitly admits Int64-to-Decimal(35,0) without loss and makes Decimal-to-Int64 StrictCast nullable.
limitations: Source review only; actual compiler, type transformer and row/block physical aggregation execution are pending.
Bounded physical window SUM is a separate F03 fix and is not covered by this normalization rule.
Final interval range overflow must remain an optional result; native controls must include cancellation after an out-of-range partial sum.
